The recent Orca Security Report has shed light on a disturbing trend in the AI industry: 99.9% of fixable AI vulnerabilities remain unpatched. This is a significant concern that requires immediate attention from developers and companies alike. 
Questions to consider: What are the potential consequences of unpatched AI vulnerabilities? How can the AI industry prioritize security? What role do developers and companies play in addressing this issue?
#AI #Security #Vulnerabilities #OrcaSecurityReport #TheWire #TechNews

slide2.title: WHAT HAPPENED
lines: Event date: 14 Jul 2026
Orca Security Report found that 99.9% of fixable AI vulnerabilities remain unpatched.
This is a significant concern for the AI industry.
The report emphasizes the need for better security measures.
As AI continues to grow, so do the potential risks.

slide3.title: WHY IT MATTERS
lines: Unpatched vulnerabilities can lead to severe consequences, including data breaches and system compromises.
The AI industry must prioritize security to mitigate these risks.
Developers and companies must work together to address this issue.
Source: TheWire.in, 14 Jul 2026

slide1.headline: UST Partners with Anthropic to Train Developers
slide1.subtitle: Partnership aims to train 20,000 developers on Claude

slide2.title: WHAT HAPPENED
lines: Event date: 13 Jul 2026
UST has partnered with Anthropic to train 20,000 developers on Claude.
This partnership aims to increase adoption and development of AI solutions.
The training program will focus on Claude, Anthropic's AI model.
The partnership is expected to last for several months.

slide3.title: WHY IT MATTERS
lines: The partnership between UST and Anthropic can lead to significant advancements in AI adoption.
Training 20,000 developers on Claude can increase the number of AI solutions developed.
The partnership highlights the growing interest in AI technology and its potential applications.
